methods.name: Stage-Progression

data.narrative:
Ulysses Robotics, a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Akhil Voorakkara, Jamie Wedderburn, Colm O'Brien, and Will O'Brien, has raised $38M to date. Valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 private companies and 1 public company (277810.KQ), with direct peer references including Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), and Walden Robotics ($1.1B, Seed).

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $38M raised as a proxy for current post-money value, applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent funding round progression, implying $76M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range of $1.1B to $1.8B. This wider peer distribution reflects the heterogeneity of robotics funding outcomes across seed through Series B stages.

Triangulation across both methods produces a valuation range of $65M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $863M. The wide dispersion reflects tension between stage-based mechanistic progression and peer-derived outcomes, with the peer set skewed toward later-stage funding rounds. Key uncertainties include the timing and structure of Ulysses' next funding event relative to peer comparables, and which subset of the peer universe most accurately reflects company-specific technology and market dynamics.
